bottleneck: Ketamine relieves depression within hours — unlike the weeks SSRIs require — yet its mechanism is disputed: NMDA receptor blockade, glutamate surge, BDNF release, and opioid-system involvement all have supporting evidence, and they point to different drug designs. Without knowing which pathway matters, developers cannot design safer, non-dissociative successors rationally, and the bladder toxicity, dissociation, and abuse potential of chronic ketamine limit its use to supervised settings. The fastest-acting antidepressant known is a blunt instrument whose sharp edge cannot be isolated from its risks.
current_state: Esketamine is approved for treatment-resistant depression; next-generation rapid antidepressants chase the mechanism without consensus on which pathway to target.
title: Ketamine's rapid antidepressant mechanism disputed
why_it_blocks: Hours-versus-weeks is the difference between saving a suicidal patient and losing them. The mechanism dispute blocks rational design of rapid antidepressants without ketamine's risks — the most urgent problem in psychiatry pharmacology.
